newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher on telecom sector.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher on telecom sector.

text.p: Brazilian shares closed up 1.08 percent, underpinned by telecommunications stocks which rose following remarks by Communications Minister Sergio Motta, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most liquid stocks ended at 9,237 points. Market turnover was 575.2 million reais ($542.6 million).
Earlier today Motta said he expected tender details for the privatization of Telesp and Embratel, two of Telebras' units, to be ready by the first quarter of 1998.

Motta also said the government was not considering a telecommunications rate increase, but he noted it was seeking to establish "true" tariff levels for different services in the telecom industry in the run-up to the sector's sell-off.
Analysts said the upgrade of Brazil's long-term foreign currency debt rating by Standard & Poor's Corp also helped to improve market sentiment.
Bellwether Telebras gained 1.61 percent to 113.40 reais, while its common stock rose 1.57 percent, closing at 110.20 reais.
Traders also pointed out that Motta's comments on Telebras subscription receipts had no impact on Telebras stock.
Trade in the receipts was halted today after the Communications Minister said he would back a court ruling against the firm in a subscription receipt dispute.
Telebras is awaiting a final ruling on whether holders of the subscription receipts will be issued preferred shares from a 1990 public offering.
Telebras receipts fell 12 percent before trading was suspended.

Analysts said the market could continue firming on Thursday, especially if the Chamber of Deputies, which was due to vote later today on the government's administrative reform in a first round, approves the bill.
The Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index .IEE, comprising the nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector, rose 1.11 percent, ending at 2,506 points.
